result.rationale: The diff adds next/previous actions that set offset and call group.findMembers(), an async Discourse.ajax call with no cancellation or in-flight guard (group.js findMembers). Concurrent rapid clicks can cause out-of-order responses, and the then() callback unconditionally setProperties user_count/offset/members, so a stale response can overwrite a newer one. Mechanism is verifiable in the diff, though the practical impact depends on user behavior.

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces pagination actions (`next`/`previous`) that update `group.offset` and immediately call `group.findMembers()` (admin-group.js.es6). `findMembers()` performs an async `Discourse.ajax(...)` and then unconditionally `setProperties({ ... offset: result.meta.offset, members: ... })` on the model (group.js). There is no request cancellation, no sequencing token, and no guard to ignore stale responses, so rapid clicks can create multiple in-flight requests whose responses may arrive out of order and overwrite newer page state (wrong `members`/`offset` displayed). The actions also compute the next offset using current `group.get("user_count")`, which can be stale relative to what the server will return, potentially compounding page drift when combined with out-of-order updates.
